sections.html: Se laisser + infinitive means "to let oneself be / do something". It suggests passivity, giving in, or allowing something to happen, without resistance.

sections.heading: Two meanings
sections.html:
1. Allowing something to be done to oneself (passive): - Il s'est laissé convaincre. — He let himself be convinced. - Ne te laisse pas faire ! — Don't let them push you around! - Elle s'est laissé séduire par l'offre. — She let herself be won over by the offer. - Je me suis laissé surprendre par la pluie. — I got caught in the rain.

2. Letting oneself do something / giving in (active): - Je me suis laissé tomber sur le canapé. — I let myself drop onto the sofa. - Il se laisse aller. — He's letting himself go (neglecting himself). - Elle s'est laissé emporter par la colère. — She got carried away by anger. - Laisse-toi aller ! — Let yourself go! / Relax!

sections.heading: Agreement (modern rule)
sections.html: Since the 1990 spelling reform, laissé followed by an infinitive is invariable (like fait): Elle s'est laissé convaincre. Older usage made it agree if the subject performs the infinitive action (Elle s'est laissée tomber), so you'll see both. Using the invariable form is always correct.

sections.heading: Common expressions
sections.html:
Expression Meaning
se laisser faire to let oneself be pushed around, not resist
se laisser aller to let oneself go, relax / neglect oneself
se laisser tenter to give in to temptation (Je me suis laissé tenter par un dessert.)
se laisser abattre to get discouraged (Ne te laisse pas abattre ! — Don't let it get you down!)
se laisser marcher sur les pieds to let people walk all over you
se laisser emporter to get carried away
se laisser vivre to take it easy
se laisser pousser la barbe / les cheveux to grow a beard / one's hair
se laisser prendre to be taken in, fooled
ne pas se laisser démonter to keep one's cool

sections.heading: Comparison
sections.html:
Faire Se faire Laisser Se laisser
cause someone to do have something done to oneself let someone do let oneself be / do
Je fais chanter Paul. Je me fais coiffer. Je laisse Paul chanter. Je me laisse coiffer. (I let them do my hair)

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I gave in to temptation and bought the shoes."
exercises.answer: *Je me suis laissé tenter et j'ai acheté les chaussures.*

exercises.prompt: Translate: "She let herself be convinced by the salesman."
exercises.answer: *Elle s'est laissé convaincre par le vendeur.*

exercises.prompt: Which is the difference between *Il s'est fait avoir* and *Il s'est laissé avoir*?
exercises.answer: *Il s'est fait avoir* = he got fooled (focus on the event). *Il s'est laissé avoir* = he let himself be fooled (suggests he could have avoided it; passivity, naivety).
